description: We are Berrak and Nisa Nur, third-year Industrial Engineering students interested in data analysis, optimization, and software development. We participated in TEKNOFEST in 2024 and 2025, gaining experience in teamwork and project development. We enjoy exploring new technologies and using data to solve real-world problems. Through NASA Space Apps Challenge, we hope to learn, collaborate, and turn our ideas into a meaningful project.
summary:
Field Shift is a free, web-based agricultural decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into practical, three-year crop rotation strategies to help farmers improve soil health, manage water resources, and reduce environmental risks.

Our platform integrates NASA POWER climate and soil moisture data, SRTM elevation data, and MODIS vegetation observations with local agricultural conditions and farmer preferences. It evaluates 73 crop rotation strategies, selects suitable cover crops, and compares alternatives using eight sustainability and agricultural performance indicators.

Unlike conventional crop recommendation tools, Field Shift allows farmers to explore different scenarios, apply irrigation and crop restrictions, and understand the trade-offs between soil protection, nitrogen balance, water consumption, and climate risks. An interactive 3D visualization makes the results easier to understand.

By making NASA data accessible through a free, bilingual, mobile-friendly platform, Field Shift supports more informed agricultural decisions and contributes to sustainable farming, soil conservation, and climate resilience.
details:
Field Shift – NASA-Powered Agricultural Decision Support

Project Overview

Field Shift is a free, bilingual, web-based agricultural decision-support platform developed by Team TARSA for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our goal is to transform NASA Earth observation data into practical, scientifically informed crop rotation strategies that help farmers protect soil health, optimize water usage, and adapt to changing climate conditions.

Traditional agricultural practices often rely on repeated cultivation of the same crops, leaving fields exposed to erosion, nutrient depletion, and environmental stress. Field Shift addresses these challenges by allowing farmers to compare alternative three-year crop rotation strategies based on their specific geographic location, soil conditions, available resources, and agricultural priorities.

How Does It Work?

The platform integrates multiple NASA Earth observation datasets:

  • NASA POWER: Provides 20 years of historical climate information (2004–2023), including precipitation, temperature, frost events, extreme heat, and soil moisture estimates.
  • NASA SRTM: Supplies elevation and terrain information to estimate field slope and support erosion analysis.
  • NASA MODIS: Provides satellite vegetation observations to identify periods when agricultural land may remain uncovered.
  • USDA Cropland Data Layer: Identifies historical crop patterns for supported locations in the United States.

Farmers enter their location, current crop rotation, soil characteristics, irrigation availability, and agricultural priorities.

Our optimization engine evaluates 73 different three-year crop rotation strategies, considering 10 main crops and 13 cover crop options. Each strategy is assessed using eight indicators, including soil coverage, nitrogen balance, organic matter, water requirements, pest and disease cycles, climate risks, market considerations, and animal feed potential.

The platform presents multiple alternatives, explaining their potential benefits, supporting NASA data, uncertainties, and agricultural risks.

Innovation and Key Features

One of Field Shift's main innovations is its ability to compare complete multi-year agricultural strategies rather than recommending individual crops.

Our interactive Decision Lab allows farmers to introduce practical constraints, including maximum annual irrigation limits and required or excluded crops. The platform automatically filters unsuitable strategies and uses multi-objective Pareto analysis to visualize trade-offs between water consumption, soil protection, nitrogen balance, and climate risks.

If no strategy satisfies the farmer's requirements, the system explicitly explains why instead of generating unrealistic recommendations.

Additionally, our interactive 3D agricultural visualization allows users to explore crop development, terrain characteristics, soil conditions, and environmental changes throughout a 36-month agricultural cycle.

Demonstrated Results

In our Nebraska case study, historical USDA data showed seven consecutive years of corn cultivation.

Our evaluation produced the following comparative scores:

  • Current farming strategy: 46/100
  • Existing rotation with winter cover crops: 63/100
  • Alternative rotation with suitable cover crops: 83/100

The model estimated that approximately 197 mm of annual precipitation reached uncovered soil under the existing strategy. The proposed cover-crop strategy substantially reduced this estimated exposure while improving nitrogen balance.

However, the platform also identified additional soil-water consumption associated with cover crops, demonstrating our commitment to presenting realistic trade-offs rather than one-sided recommendations.

Technologies and Development Tools

Field Shift was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for its web interface and optimization algorithms.

We used Three.js for interactive 3D visualization, Python and Node.js scripts for data acquisition and processing, and GitHub Pages for public deployment.

NASA POWER data services, SRTM elevation datasets, MODIS vegetation services, and USDA agricultural datasets form the foundation of our analytical system.

The platform also includes automated tests for optimization constraints, Pareto calculations, and result consistency.

Claude (Anthropic) assisted with website coding and data retrieval, with outputs reviewed by the team. No AI-generated visualizations were used.

The application operates directly in modern web browsers without requiring specialized hardware, user registration, or paid subscriptions.

Intended Impact and Future Development

Field Shift aims to make satellite-based agricultural intelligence accessible to farmers, agricultural advisors, researchers, and students worldwide.

By supporting informed crop rotation decisions, our platform has the potential to contribute to soil conservation, more efficient water management, improved agricultural resilience, and sustainable land use.

We recognize that satellite measurements and crop parameters have limitations. Our scores are comparative decision-support indicators, not guaranteed yield or profitability predictions. The platform transparently communicates these uncertainties, and field validation remains an essential next step.

Future development will incorporate NASA SMAP soil moisture observations, GPM precipitation data, higher-resolution Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery, and validation with local agricultural experts.

Our vision is to bridge the gap between NASA's scientific Earth observation capabilities and everyday agricultural decision-making, making sustainable farming more accessible, understandable, and data-driven.
